questions.q: What is the characteristic sex predilection stated for Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome?
questions.exp: Under Features of WPW Syndrome: 'M > F'. (Book p413)

questions.q: Which electrocardiographic finding is NOT part of the classic ECG pattern of WPW syndrome listed on page 413?
opts: Short PR interval and delta waves
Near normal QRS with secondary ST and T wave changes
questions.exp: ECG features: Normal P wave, Short PR interval, Delta waves, Near normal QRS, Secondary ST & T wave changes. PR is short, not prolonged. (Book p413)

questions.q: The electrophysiological mechanism of WPW syndrome involves an aberrant accessory pathway known as the Bundle of ____ that causes pre-excitation of the ventricle.
questions.exp: Mechanism: Bundle of Kent: Aberrant pathway -> Pre-excitation of ventricle. (Book p413)

questions.q: Match each WPW type to its 12-lead ECG appearance and antegrade conduction pathway — 1) Concealed WPW 12-lead ECG 2) Concealed WPW antegrade limb 3) Manifest WPW 12-lead ECG 4) Manifest WPW antegrade limb … A) Normal B) Via AV node C) Abnormal D) Via Bundle of Kent (BOK)
questions.exp: Types table: Concealed: 12-lead ECG Normal, Antegrade via AV node; Manifest: 12-lead ECG Abnormal, Antegrade via Bundle of Kent (BOK). (Book p413)

questions.q: Which two arrhythmias can be triggered by a premature atrial complex (PAC) in both concealed and manifest WPW syndrome?
opts: Sinus arrest and Mobitz type II block
questions.exp: Under Arrhythmias triggered by PAC: Both Concealed and Manifest forms can develop Orthodromic AVRT and A.fib. (Book p413)

questions.q: Which statement accurately reflects the clinical prognosis of Atrial Fibrillation occurring in concealed versus manifest WPW on page 413?
opts: True — In concealed WPW, A.fib carries a bad prognosis and responds only to DC cardioversion, whereas manifest WPW has a better prognosis due to early diagnosis
True — In concealed WPW, A.fib responds promptly to intravenous verapamil and carries an excellent prognosis
False — Manifest WPW carries a uniformly fatal prognosis because early diagnosis cannot be achieved
False — A.fib in concealed WPW resolves spontaneously without requiring electrical cardioversion
questions.exp: Prognosis: Concealed: A.fib: Bad prognosis, responds only to DC Cardioversion. Manifest: Better prognosis (d/t early diagnosis). (Book p413)

questions.q: In the classification of WPW by accessory pathway location, which is the most common anatomical subtype?
questions.exp: Left sided WPW is designated as Type A (m/c). (Book p414)

questions.q: A 22-year-old male undergoes a routine sports physical. ECG shows a short PR interval, small delta wave, and a tall positive R wave in lead V1. What type of WPW is present and what is the direction of ventricular activation?
opts: Left-sided WPW (Type A); Conduction proceeds from Left to Right
Right-sided WPW (Type B); Conduction proceeds from Right to Left
Concealed WPW; Conduction proceeds solely through the AV node
Mahaim fiber pre-excitation; Conduction proceeds from Apex to Base
questions.exp: Left sided WPW (Type A): Delta wave small (less myocardial activation), Conduction Lt -> Rt, V1 lead: +ve tall R wave + delta wave. (Book p414)

questions.q: An ECG reveals a large delta wave with a predominantly negative R wave / deep QS complex in lead V1. Which accessory pathway variant does this morphology indicate?
opts: Right-sided WPW (Type B) with Right-to-Left conduction
Left-sided WPW (Type A) with Left-to-Right conduction
Anterior fascicular block with isolated septal pre-excitation
Typical AVNRT with slow-fast dual AV nodal physiology
questions.exp: Right sided WPW (Type B): Delta wave large, Conduction Rt -> Lt, V1 lead: -ve R wave + delta wave. (Book p414)

questions.q: Match each WPW variant to its delta wave size and lead V1 morphology — 1) Type A left-sided delta wave 2) Type A lead V1 appearance 3) Type B right-sided delta wave 4) Type B lead V1 appearance … A) Small (less myocardial activation) B) Positive tall R wave C) Large D) Negative R wave
questions.exp: Type A: Small delta, +ve tall R wave in V1. Type B: Large delta, -ve R wave in V1. (Book p414)

questions.q: In manifest WPW, the lack of delay across the Bundle of Kent initiates early ventricular pre-excitation (producing the short PR and delta wave), after which the AV nodal impulse ____ to complete a near-normal QRS duration.
questions.exp: Manifest WPW diagram: Bundle of Kent (no delay) -> Pre-excitation (Short PR, delta wave); AV node -> Catch up -> Near normal QRS complex. (Book p414)

questions.q: In a patient known to have concealed WPW who develops acute Atrial Fibrillation, what is the indicated management on page 414?
questions.exp: Under Management of Concealed WPW: If AVRT -> Adenosine -> Refer to Electrophysiologist; If A.fib -> Synchronised DC cardioversion. (Book p414)

questions.q: What is the definitive curative treatment (Definitive Rx) for manifest WPW syndrome identified on early diagnosis?
opts: Surgical division of the AV node
questions.exp: Under Manifest WPW management: Early Dx -> Catheter ablation: Definitive Rx. (Book p414)

questions.q: In manifest WPW, what electrocardiographic pattern is observed after acute tachycardia (AVRT or A.fib) is successfully terminated?
opts: True — Conversion reveals sinus rhythm accompanied by the baseline delta wave, after which the patient is referred to an electrophysiologist
True — Conversion produces permanent complete AV block with an idioventricular escape pacemaker
False — Following cardioversion, the delta wave disappears permanently from all subsequent ECGs
False — Manifest WPW cannot be converted with adenosine or DC cardioversion
questions.exp: In the flowchart for manifest WPW: AVRT treated with Adenosine and A.fib treated with Synchronised DC cardioversion both yield 'Sinus rhythm + delta wave', followed by 'Refer to Electrophysiologist'. (Book p414)
